skill.name: executor-plan-regression
skill.description: Audits drafted plan sets for specification coverage, cross-plan dependencies, and interface drift before execution. Coordinates documented repairs and independent re-audits.
skill.summary: Review related plans, repair document defects, and verify the Executor planning gate before execution.
skill.author: atri10

security_audit.summary: All 243 static findings are false positives involving Markdown backticks, fixed companion-tool paths, or document-review prose. No evidence found of prompt injection, credential exfiltration, or malicious host reconnaissance in the four reviewed files. Referenced companion scripts are absent from this skill, so their implementation and runtime behavior were not verified.

content.user_title: Audit and Repair Plans Before Execution
content.value_statement: Separate plans can hide missing requirements, incompatible interfaces, and broken dependencies. This skill reviews the complete plan set and coordinates repairs with independent verification.
actual_capabilities: Builds requirement coverage tables across the complete plan set and identifies missing or invalid coverage claims.
Checks assumptions and consumed artifacts against producers, interface contracts, and execution order.
Reviews interface literals, global constraints, shared file writes, and vocabulary across plans.
Uses plan-lint output and verifies that cited architecture and specification documents exist.
Directs scoped plan repairs with evidence logs and routes contract amendments to the controller.
Defines independent re-audits, finding closure tables, human waiver records, and execution-gate verification.
limitations: Requires companion Executor tools that are referenced but not included in these four files.
Reviews and repairs planning documents, not implementation code or deployed systems.
Requires file access, command execution, Git, and separate agent dispatches for the complete workflow.
Caps audit rounds at three and requires human decisions for unresolved findings or waivers.

use_cases.title: Check Plans Before Implementation
use_cases.description: Review a drafted plan set for missing requirements and unresolved producer dependencies before developers begin task execution.

use_cases.title: Coordinate Contract Repairs
use_cases.description: Assign cross-plan fixes, record specification or interface amendments, and obtain independent confirmation without allowing repairers to grade themselves.

use_cases.title: Verify Readiness Evidence
use_cases.description: Compare latest audit reports, repair logs, and human waiver records before confirming that the initiative can enter execution.

prompt_templates.title: Check Audit Readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Use executor-plan-regression to check whether my drafted plan set is ready for auditing. Identify missing specifications, contracts, companion tools, and required inputs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner: confirm prerequisites before starting the workflow.

prompt_templates.title: Audit the Complete Plan Set
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit each drafted plan against the complete plan set, specification, and cited interface contracts. Use the supplied auditor template and report all nine checks.
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate: run the first audit round after drafting finishes.

prompt_templates.title: Repair Assigned Findings
prompt_templates.prompt: Coordinate repairs for the failed audit findings. Assign one owner per finding, keep repairs within document boundaries, and dispatch independent re-auditors with repair diffs.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: repair plan defects and verify closure.

prompt_templates.title: Recheck Changed Plans Before Execution
prompt_templates.prompt: Re-enter plan regression for the changed plans and their affected dependencies. Verify coverage, contract amendments, latest audit references, and human waivers before clearing execution.
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced: handle plan or specification changes during an initiative.

output_examples.input: Review two drafted plans where a later plan consumes an artifact that no earlier plan produces.
output: Illustrative audit result: failed because a required producer is missing.
Coverage review: one requirement has no implementing task.
Dependency review: the later plan consumes an unresolved artifact.
Repair routing: assign the producer correction and request an independent re-audit.

output_examples.input: Re-audit a repaired plan whose interface literal now matches its contract.
output: Illustrative closure result: the prior interface finding is addressed using evidence from the repaired plan.
Impact review: coverage, dependencies, ordering, and lint were checked again.
Readiness result: mark the plan clean only after independent audit success and the companion gate check.

best_practices: Provide every plan, its specification, cited contracts, and current lint output before dispatching auditors.
Keep repairers and re-auditors independent, and preserve each completed audit round.
Review companion tools before running them, inspect repair diffs, and record human waivers explicitly.
anti_patterns: Auditing one plan without the other plans that supply or consume its outputs.
Removing requirements or weakening exact interface values to make an audit pass.
Marking a plan clean from a repair log without a fresh independent audit.

faq.question: What does this skill review?
faq.answer: It reviews plan documents against specifications, interface contracts, other plans, and lint output. It does not audit implementation code.

faq.question: When should I use it?
faq.answer: Use it after drafting the complete plan set and before execution. Re-enter the phase when plans or their specifications change.

faq.question: Can it review a single plan?
faq.answer: Yes. Specification coverage, interface fidelity, lint, and skipped-phase checks still apply to a single-plan initiative.

faq.question: Does the package include the Executor commands?
faq.answer: No. The reviewed package contains instructions and three prompt templates. The referenced Executor tools must be available separately.

faq.question: Which AI tools are listed as supported?
faq.answer: The report lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code. Full orchestration also requires suitable file, shell, Git, and separate-agent access.

faq.question: What happens when findings remain after three audits?
faq.answer: The controller stops the repair loop and requests a human decision. Waivers must be explicit and recorded in initiative rulings.
